ssh.title: Remote login (SSH)
ssh.hint: Lets people sign in to this server's command line from another computer. Off by default; only the local network can reach it.
ssh.notInstalled: Off. Turning it on installs the SSH server first.
ssh.cantInstall: The SSH server isn't installed, and NoCapOS can't install it on this system.
ssh.offMsg: The SSH server stops and Shield closes its port. Sessions already open may be cut off. The SSH server stays installed.
ssh.overriddenHint: A settings file the SSH server reads before NoCapOS's own sets: {names}.
ssh.fw.noneHint: Shield's firewall isn't set up, so every device that can reach this server can try to log in.
ssh.fw.offHint: With the firewall off, every device that can reach this server can try to log in, not only the local network.
ssh.fw.onMsg: Shield's firewall starts with a rule that lets the local network reach remote login. You stay connected.
ssh.fw.blockedHint: Shield's rule for remote login was removed, so nobody can connect.
ssh.fw.fixed: Shield lets the local network in again
ssh.fw.okLan: Open to the local network only.
ssh.fw.okOutside: Open to the local network, and rate-limited from anywhere else.
ssh.connectHint: Type one of these in a terminal on the other computer.
ssh.noAddress: This server has no network address right now.
ssh.whoHint: The root account can never log in over SSH.
ssh.passwordOn: Signing in with a password is allowed. SSH keys are safer.
ssh.passwordOff: Only SSH keys can sign in.
ssh.passwordKeys: There are SSH keys now. Consider turning password login off.
ssh.guard.sshd: Three tries per connection, and addresses that keep failing are blocked for a while.
ssh.guard.fw: Three tries per connection, and Shield slows down addresses that connect too often.
ssh.outside: Allow from outside the home network
ssh.outsideHint: Off: only devices on the local network can connect. On: anyone on the internet who can reach this server can try.
ssh.outsideLocalOnly: This server lets only its own screen open NoCapOS (Settings, General, This Screen & Access), so this stays off.
ssh.outsideMsg: Anyone on the internet who can reach this server can then try to log in. Use SSH keys and turn password login off first. Shield rate-limits the port.
ssh.keys.title: SSH keys
ssh.keys.hint: Public keys that can sign in to your account over remote login, without a password.
ssh.keys.name: Name
ssh.keys.removeMsg: This key can no longer sign in to {user}'s account.
ssh.keys.tooBig: That file is too big to be a public key.
ssh.keys.othersHint: As an administrator you can see and remove anyone's keys.
